title: Introducing FOCUS 1.4: Invoice Reconciliation, Commitment Details, and Specification Maturity
authors_or_org: Shawn Alpay and Matt Cowsert / FinOps Foundation
supported_claim: FOCUS 1.4 introduces Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets and expanded commitment/correction semantics.
limitations: Release description does not establish provider adoption or current validator support; announcement future promises are not treated as completed.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer

title: FOCUS 1.4: Billed Cost
supported_claim: Billed cost is invoice-basis cost in billing currency; covered amounts are not double-counted as usage; final invoice matching is subject to rounding tolerance.
limitations: FOCUS semantics must not be imposed on nonconformant native exports; invoice-basis costs do not establish settlement timing.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer

title: FOCUS 1.4: Effective Cost
supported_claim: Effective cost attributes cost to use/commitments in charge period; complete covering/covered relationships conserve billed/effective totals across covering period, not arbitrary monthly subsets.
limitations: Does not prescribe an enterprise financial-reporting policy or prove that provider data covers both sides of a commitment.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer

title: FOCUS 1.4: Invoice Reconciliation
supported_claim: Invoice Detail identifiers bridge usage, invoice amounts, tax, and divergent billing/payment currency grains.
limitations: Example SQL is not a complete production key/coverage policy; actual payments are separate evidence.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer

title: FOCUS 1.4: Correction Handling
supported_claim: Replacement snapshots, additive deltas and ledger reversals/re-entries require different aggregation semantics.
limitations: Native non-FOCUS sources may use different delivery scope or omit correction metadata.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer

title: FOCUS 1.4: Rounding Variance Tolerance
supported_claim: Invoice tolerance equals max(100 subunits, 0.5 sqrt(rows) subunits), including a USD 1 floor.
limitations: A tolerance pass does not prove exact equality or that small missing charges are harmless; no statistical validation of the tolerance is independently established here.
license_status: CC BY 4.0 stated in page footer
